Page 1 item I FMV of all assets at end of year $2,723,259,744. Part IX line 5 net noncharitable-use assets $2,667,605,428; line 6 MIR $133,380,271. Part X: tax on investment income $21,037,979; recoveries $11,080,588; line 7 distributable amount $123,422,880. record.finding: In July 2026 Buffett excluded the Gates Foundation from his annual Berkshire stock gifts for the first time in 20 years, directing 9M Class B shares to the Susan Thompson Buffett Foundation and 1M each to the Sherwood, Howard G. Buffett and NoVo foundations, pending the Gates Foundation's WilmerHale review of its Epstein ties. He aims to dispose of all Berkshire shares by 2034.

foundation.name: Fangmei Education Development Fund (Longyan, Fujian) - a local government-administered education fund, not a private foundation

record.finding: Donated 500 million yuan (about USD 77M) in June 2021 to set up the Fangmei Education Development Fund in his hometown Longyan, Fujian, named after his grandmothers; announced during the post-crackdown 'common prosperity' charity wave among Chinese tech founders.
Longyan Education Bureau announced May 2023 an additional 200 million yuan (about USD 28.9M) donation to the same fund.

Foundation's 2024 activity report: total mecenat activity 85.1M EUR (life sciences 16.1M, crafts/metiers d'art 4.4M, choral 3M, solidarity 11.4M; remainder incl. large operations such as Notre-Dame). 2023: 68.6M EUR (prizes 8.6M, gifts 55.5M).

Foundation is a top contributor to Notre-Dame de Paris reconstruction with a 100M EUR gift (press release 3 June 2024). Forbes: L'Oreal plus the family agreed to donate about USD 226M for Notre-Dame after the 2019 fire.

Endowment not stated in accessible 2024 report summary; French Wikipedia cites a Paris Match (2017) figure of roughly 900M EUR budget/endowment and ~500M EUR distributed cumulatively by 2017 - secondary, not verified against foundation accounts.

foundation.name: Reliance Foundation (chaired by Nita Ambani; CSR arm of Reliance Industries Ltd)

record.finding: RIL Integrated Annual Report 2024-25: 'In FY 2024-25, Reliance Industries Limited spent INR 2,156 Crore towards CSR' (approx. 21.56 billion INR); Reliance Foundation claims 8.6 crore lives impacted since 2010. Prior year FY2023-24: INR 1,592 crore (press).

Electoral bonds disclosure (Mar 2024): Qwik Supply Chain Pvt Ltd, the third-largest bond buyer at INR 410 crore (2021-22 to 2023-24; INR 385 cr to BJP, INR 25 cr to Shiv Sena), was reported by Reuters and The Reporters' Collective to be affiliated with Reliance via directors/addresses; RIL stated Qwik 'is not a subsidiary of any Reliance entity'.
Foundation is funded by and reports through the listed company (RIL) rather than by the family personally; spend is statutory corporate CSR.

2021: Bitfinex/Tether (of which Devasini is CFO/co-owner) paid USD 18.5M to settle the New York Attorney General's lawsuit over the use of Tether reserves to cover Bitfinex losses in 2018 (company-level settlement).
1995: accused of software piracy by Microsoft in Italy; agreed to pay a fine of one million lire to avoid prosecution (per Corriere del Ticino via Wikipedia).
Lived in Lugano 2017-2023; Tether signed an MoU ('Plan B') with the city of Lugano promoting crypto adoption - corporate/civic partnership, not charitable giving.

foundation.name: David H Koch Charitable Foundation
foundation.note: Which foundation is hers: ProPublica API searches for 'David H Koch Foundation' and 'Julia Koch' return (1) David H Koch Charitable Foundation, Wichita KS, EIN 48-0926946, a 501(c)(3) private foundation filing Form 990-PF, on which Julia F Koch is listed as Director/President/Secretary ($0 comp) -- this is the entity recorded here; and (2) Julia Koch Family Foundation, Wichita KS, EIN 92-1599313, tax-exempt since Feb 2023, but it is a 501(c)(4) social-welfare organization that files Form 990 (not 990-PF), so no 990-PF payout metrics exist for it: its FY2024 Form 990 (filed Nov 14 2025) shows total assets $14,205,290, expenses $36,706,825, revenue $754,778, after a $55,000,000 contribution in FY2023; Julia F Koch is a Director. Neither entity is large: the 990-PF filer here had only $1.5M FMV at end of 2024, so status is 'secondary' -- Julia Koch's wealth is not held in a foundation she controls that files a 990-PF. Figures for the David H Koch Charitable Foundation Form 990-PF FY ending Dec 2024, filed Nov 14 2025, read from ProPublica full-text rendering (full_text/202533189349101043/IRS990PF): page 1 item I FMV of all assets at end of year $1,512,449 (noncharitable-use assets in Part IX are an average over the year, hence larger than year-end FMV: line 5 $2,729,995; line 6 MIR $136,500). Part X line 7 distributable amount $134,368 (from Part XII line 1). Part XI line 4 qualifying distributions $2,108,295. Part XII: lines 2a/2b = 0, 6b = 0, 6d = 0, 6f undistributed income for 2024 = 0; line 9 excess distributions carryover to 2025 $7,554,028. Part I line 13 officer/director/trustee compensation $0 (ProPublica summary also shows $0). Part VI-B 2a checkbox state not rendered in text; exciseTaxOnUndistributed=false inferred from Part XII zeros. payoutRate = 2,108,295 / 1,512,449 = 1.394 (foundation is spending down). Not a private operating foundation.
